## Context

**What this card is.** The visual half of the alert loop. t75 shipped the
stack (prometheus + alertmanager + grafana, ports 9090/9093/3000), t76 shipped
the scrape config and the alerts authority, and t79 wires the emitters - but
nothing a reviewer can LOOK AT exists until this card. Two files are the whole
envelope: `observability/dashboard.json` (three panels that answer the three
questions the alert set poses: is creation working, is it failing, is the
database fallback engaged) and `observability/collector.yaml` (the
configuration half of the OPTIONAL OTel collector that t75 left as a commented
block - present as a documented option, NOT as an enabled service). This card
ships no alert, no scrape config, no backend code, no incident record and no
evidence.

**Measured base state (measured at groom at BASE 09bca7c, not assumed).**
`observability/` exists and holds EXACTLY four files: `README.md` and
`compose.yaml` (t75) plus `prometheus.yml` and `alerts.yaml` (t76, merged -
`git ls-tree 09bca7c observability/` lists exactly those four blobs). Neither
of this card's two files exists at BASE in any branch. `core.autocrlf=true` is
set repo-wide and `.gitattributes` is absent (both measured at groom), which is
why ac5 checks the WORKING COPY for CRLF and non-ASCII on files that are NEW in
this delta (the t82-disclosed difference from t80's blob-level leg). The
validators this card pins are `python3` (stdlib `json`/`re`) for the dashboard
and `python3` + PyYAML for the collector (measured: python3 3.12.3, PyYAML
6.0.1 under WSL; PyYAML is also a committed backend dependency) - the same
pair the merged t76 and t82 fences pin. `node_modules/` is gitignored and
measured ABSENT in this worktree, so no node library is pinned anywhere in
these fences, and the survey draft's "a JSON validator is available with no new
dependency (`node -e` with the root `node_modules`)" is corrected to the
measured python3 pair. `docs/state/merge_test_index.json` holds 283 stored
gates and ZERO of them name `dashboard.json`, `collector.yaml` or this card's
surface (the two index entries containing the word "collector" are t75's
compose-block fences, which this card's delta leaves byte-clean). There is
therefore no pin switchover and no index edit for this card.

**The metric names are extracted, never copied.** `observability/alerts.yaml`
is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every alert and metric name in this
milestone, and it carries a machine-readable inventory line (the doubled
`# # METRIC-INVENTORY:` marker) with the four declared names and instrument
types. ac2's probe READS that line at run time, extracts the name set, and
asserts (a) every metric token in every panel `expr` is in the extracted set
and (b) no extracted name is left unvisualised. The card therefore does not
restate the inventory anywhere - if t76 ever changes a name the fence follows
the file, which is the whole point of single-source authority. The candidate
measured at groom extracted the four-name set and matched it exactly, and the
deliberate mutant that swaps the fallback panel's series for an invented name -
and the liveness-shaped `up == 0` mutant that this milestone explicitly
removed - were each RED by ac2. **Why the coverage leg exists:** a dashboard
that shows three of four declared series is a silent gap, and a gap in the
fallback panel is the exact defect the t76 Option B decision removed.

**The dashboard URL is READ from the merged annotation, not invented.**
t76's alert annotations already promise a loopback Grafana URL. If this card's
dashboard carried any other uid or title, that annotation would point at a
dashboard that does not exist - a reviewer clicks it and lands on a 404. ac4
therefore extracts the annotation URL from the merged file, requires it to be
single-valued and loopback, and requires this dashboard's `uid` and
slugified `title` to reproduce the `/d/<uid>/<slug>` pair it carries. The
candidate measured at groom reproduces it exactly; the uid-contradicting and
title-contradicting mutants were each RED. The card edits NO annotation -
per the survey's own rule, if the annotation ever needs a change this card
reports a follow-up rather than editing t76's file (one writer per file).

**Why the collector file is honest about being inert.** t75's compose file
carries the `otel-collector` / `loki` / `tempo` block COMMENTED OUT and records
it as a deliberate limitation; t87 restates that limitation for traces. A
collector config that reads like a running service would be the fake this
milestone exists to remove, so ac3 requires the file's own text to state that
it is NOT ENABLED, to name `compose.yaml`, and to name the `otel-collector`
service it corresponds to - and it verifies the compose side too: the block
must STILL be commented there, so the correspondence claim cannot be a lie.
The leg is non-vacuous by construction: ac3's probe REJECTS a file with no
NOT-ENABLED sentence, a file that never names `compose.yaml`, and a YAML that
parses but carries no collector vocabulary at all. The file itself documents
the two edits that WOULD enable it (uncomment in t75's compose, mount this
file) and performs neither.

**Why exactly three panels, and why the count is asserted.** The three panels
are the three questions the t76 alert set poses. ac1 asserts EXACTLY three
panels with a title and a datasource reference each and a non-empty `expr`,
and it FAILS on a fourth panel - a dashboard that quietly grows an
`up == 0` "liveness" tile reintroduces the liveness-wearing-a-fallback-name
defect t76 named and removed. The negative controls are the point: the same
legs must REJECT a four-panel dashboard, a title-less dashboard, a
datasource-less dashboard and a dashboard missing the fallback panel.

**Single-source doctrine and the cross-card boundaries (hard, fenced where the
fence reads only this card's own files plus merged read-only authorities).**

- **Alert and metric names belong to t76.** `observability/alerts.yaml` is the
  authority; this card CITES it by path and by the inventory key and restates
  no name in prose or in a fence literal. ac2 enforces the citation
  mechanically by extracting from that file at run time. ac5 fences
  `observability/alerts.yaml` (and `prometheus.yml`) byte-clean.
- **Incident-ID authority belongs to t83.** This card creates no `incidents/`
  directory, names no incident ID, and fences nothing under
  `incident-response/`; ac5 lists `incident-response` as a frozen path.
- **t81 owns `responder-task.md`/`response.schema.json`/`validate_response.py`;
  t82 owns `autonomy-policy.yaml`, `runbooks/rollback.sh` and
  `runbooks/verify-recovery.sh`.** This card neither fences their creation nor
  duplicates their surface; its envelope is the two `observability/` files and
  nothing else.
- **t79 owns the emitters.** This card declares no instrument, no help text and
  no `backend/` path; it reads the names t76 declares and t79 implements.
- **t88 and t89 consume this output.** The report points a reviewer at this
  dashboard and the evidence map cites it; that is why the URL agreement is
  fenced rather than asserted - a broken link in a report is discovered by the
  reader, which is too late.
- **This card's envelope is exactly `observability/dashboard.json` +
  `observability/collector.yaml`.** Nothing else.

**Granularity honesty.** max_files=4 and this card uses exactly 2. max_acs=6
and this card uses 5. max_diff_lines=300 is warn-only and the groom's throwaway
candidate measured **266 added lines** across the two files (dashboard 175,
collector 91), so the cap is NOT expected to be exceeded; ac5 prints the
measured number and, if it ever exceeds 300, a WARN that the handoff must
disclose rather than a mechanism being trimmed.

**Environment honesty (the t65/t81/t82 lessons, measured at groom).** This
worktree's gitdir holds Windows-formatted paths, so every git read in ac5 goes
through `cmd.exe /c "git -C <wslpath -w form> ..."` with `</dev/null` INSIDE
the bash side (never a `2>&1` or `&` inside a cmd.exe string - the cmd
separator trap) and output `tr -d "\r"` stripped; the fence REDs loudly if
`cmd.exe` is missing rather than skipping the purity leg. The fences themselves
run under WSL bash and need only `bash`, `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `tr`, `wc`,
`cat`, `mktemp`, `base64`, `python3` (stdlib `json`/`re` plus PyYAML for the
collector probe), `cmd.exe` and `wslpath`. Every probe is materialised at run
time from a base64 literal inside the fence, so each fence body carries zero
single quotes beyond its wrapper pair, zero backticks, zero tabs and exactly
one line - the t76/t81/t82 fence shape. No fence installs anything, downloads
anything, contacts a network, or touches Docker or a live Grafana.

**Review_plan disposition.** The phase_13 review_plan verdict is
PASS_WITH_WARNINGS; what it bound on this card is the plan's
verification-command discipline: every fence a self-contained `bash -c`
one-liner, the delta-purity leg expressed against a named immutable ref and
declared NON-APPENDABLE in card text (the t73/t74/t75/t80/t81/t82 lesson), no
moving count pinned upward, no metric name or URL restated from a sibling's
authority, and `ac_hash` authored at groom (the survey card recorded only the
fence-count plan, never a digest constant).

## Acceptance criteria

Five criteria - within max_acs=6. Each is one deterministic `bash -c` one-liner
run from the repository root (worktree). All five were EXECUTED at base
09bca7c by this groom and are RED there for the named reason (see the table
under **Verification commands**). Every fence is GREEN-able: all five were
re-executed against a throwaway candidate (the two files staged under the
gitignored `build/t77/cand/` tree and copied into place, then removed), and
eight deliberate mutants were each REJECTED; the groom wrote NO product content
into the project tree and committed nothing. No fence needs Docker, an internet
connection, an install step, a live Grafana, a running Prometheus or the
`/metrics` endpoint to be implemented.

### ac1 - dashboard.json exists, parses, and carries EXACTLY the three required panels

`observability/dashboard.json` exists and parses under the pinned validator
(`python3` stdlib `json` - no node fallback, because `node_modules/` is
gitignored and measured absent). An embedded probe asserts the panel set: a
non-empty `title`, a datasource reference (top-level or per-panel), EXACTLY
three panels - no fourth tile, no missing tile - and, for each panel, a
`targets` list carrying at least one non-empty `expr`. The panel titles must
cover the three questions the alert set poses (creation rate, creation failure
rate, fallback state). The negative controls are the point: the same legs must
REJECT a four-panel dashboard, a dashboard with no title, a dashboard with no
datasource anywhere, and a dashboard that dropped the fallback panel.

### ac3 - collector.yaml is present, parses, and states that it is the documented NOT-ENABLED option

`observability/collector.yaml` exists and parses under the pinned validator
pair (`python3` + PyYAML, the merged t76/t82 pair, no node fallback). Its own
text must state that it is NOT ENABLED, must name `compose.yaml`, and must name
the `otel-collector` service it corresponds to; its YAML must carry real
collector vocabulary (receivers / processors / exporters / service /

with no NOT-ENABLED sentence, a file that never names `compose.yaml`, and a
parseable YAML with no collector vocabulary must each be REJECTED.

## Verification commands

ac_hash: sha256:95e230b7ee70e9234c1d5741347bd93f996a732a7bd2157ac4a054cee2fc6326

Five fenced commands, byte-identical to
`evidence.verification_commands.ac1..ac5` in
`docs/state/outputs/t77_definer_groom.json`. The digest is sha256 over the
`JSON.stringify` array of the five FENCED BLOCKS in ac1..ac5 order, each block
taken exactly as it sits between its ```bash fences (the `bash -c '...'`
wrapper INCLUDED) with COMPACT separators and each block CR-stripped and
trimmed - the t58/t62..t76/t80/t81/t82 recipe, so the digest covers the command
exactly as it is pasted rather than a re-derived form, and it is the same array
the handoff's `evidence.verification_commands.ac1..ac5` carries. Recomputed
from the card on disk by the groom's assembler so the digest cannot drift from
the card.

Each command is a deterministic single `bash -c` one-liner with exactly two
single quotes, no heredoc, no backtick, pure ASCII, run from the repository
root.

**BASE-pinned leg disclosure (the t73/t74/t75/t80/t81/t82 lesson, declared here
as the card text requires).** ac5's purity legs are pinned to
`BASE=09bca7cda4851bf36bae45086f904a9ef47700f9` - the explicit sha measured as
this worktree's HEAD and named in the dispatch brief, never a moving ref like
`origin/main` or `HEAD`. If the builder branches from a LATER main tip (the
normal case once siblings merge), ac5 first proves descent with
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <BASE> <actual HEAD>` and then admits phase_13
sibling CARD/mirror paths under `docs/issues/` as the DISCLOSED-CAUSE case - the
builder reports them with provenance plus the actual-base diff, and must NOT
edit the fence or the allow-list. The builder additionally reports the diff
against the actual branch base, which must be EXACTLY the two allow-listed
product files. Because ac5 pins a git base into a fence, **ac5 is
NON-APPENDABLE**: the orchestrator must exclude it from the appendable
merge-test index with the recorded reason, exactly as it did for
t73/t74/t75/t80/t81/t82 ac5 ("ac5 excluded - BASE-pinned quality/delta leg not
append-safe"). ac1-ac4 are base-independent structural fences and are
appendable candidates.

**Byte-semantics disclosure (the t60/t62/t75 CRLF lesson, adapted and
disclosed).** `core.autocrlf=true` with `.gitattributes` absent (both measured
at groom) means a fresh Windows checkout smudges LF blobs to CRLF working
bytes. t80's ac5 read the COMMITTED BLOB because its files exist in HEAD by
verify time; this card's two files are NEW in its own delta, so ac5 (and ac4's
byte leg) check the WORKING COPY for non-ASCII bytes and CRLF and their RED
messages say why. The consequence: a CRLF working copy on this card IS a RED
the builder must fix by committing LF, and the verify run's appendable replay of
ac1-ac4 reads the merged bytes (the probes read file text, which is
newline-normalised on read).

**Environment disclosure (the t65/t81/t82 lessons, measured at groom).** This
worktree's gitdir holds Windows-formatted paths, so ac5's git reads go through
`cmd.exe /c "git -C <wslpath -w path> ..."`, one logical operation per
invocation, with `</dev/null` on the bash side and output `tr -d "\r"`-stripped;
the fence REDs if `cmd.exe` is missing instead of skipping the purity leg. No
cmd.exe string here contains `2>&1`, a bare `&`, or `/dev/null` (the cmd
separator trap). The builder's own git/npm/npx calls follow the same rule. The
probes are base64 literals materialised into a `mktemp -d` scratch directory
inside the fence, so no fence body contains a single quote, a backtick, a tab or
a newline. The probes were verified byte-identical to their `build/t77/src/`
sources after base64 decoding at groom.

**No-network / no-runtime disclosure.** No fence starts a server, binds a port,
runs Docker, opens a Grafana session, or contacts any address - loopback or
otherwise. The dashboard is validated as a committed ARTIFACT (parse + shape +
correspondence), never as a running page; that is also why no live-Grafana
check is promised anywhere in this card. Nothing this card writes is executed.

  datasource reference; `uid` and `title` that reproduce the loopback URL the
  merged t76 alert annotations carry; EXACTLY three panels - expense creation
  rate, creation failure rate, database fallback state - each with a

  t76 inventory, and every inventory name visualised somewhere on the board).
- Files: `observability/collector.yaml` (NEW - the ONE collector file: valid
  YAML, 2-space indent, `true`/`false` booleans; its own text states that it is
  NOT ENABLED and that it corresponds to the COMMENTED `otel-collector` block
  of `observability/compose.yaml`; real collector vocabulary (receivers /
  processors / exporters / service), loopback-only endpoints, no credential, no
  cloud endpoint, no TODO/TBD/placeholder; it enables nothing and mounts
  nothing).
- **Exactly 2 files** (max_files=4 is the ceiling, this card uses 2). One
  filename per surface: a `dashboard.yaml` or `collector.yml` twin is the
  split-brain the t81 W3 lesson names, and ac5 FAILS it.
- **No edit to `observability/compose.yaml`, `prometheus.yml`, `alerts.yaml` or
  `README.md`.** This card reads them. If the dashboard URL annotation or the
  unmounted-`alerts.yaml` follow-up needs a change, the card REPORTS a follow-up
  rather than editing t75's or t76's file - one writer per file.
- **No metric name or dashboard URL is invented or restated.**
  `observability/alerts.yaml` is the single source; ac2 extracts names from it
  at run time and ac4 extracts the URL, so the card and its fences carry no
  copy that could drift.
- **No hosted Grafana, no cloud datasource, no remote URL, no credential.** The
  datasource is the local Prometheus on t75's pinned band; the dashboard JSON
  contains no secret and no real password.
- **No live Grafana execution, no Docker, no network call, no new dependency, no
  install step in any fence.** The dashboard is validated as a committed
  artifact; nothing in this milestone renders it in a browser.
- **No backend, contract, or agent-surface change.** No `backend/` edit (t79
  owns the emitters), no `openapi.yaml` edit (FROZEN), no
  `incident-response/` or `incidents/` path (t80-t83), no `ops/` edit (t85), no
  `docs/criteria/` edit.
- **Both files are pure ASCII, LF-only, English, line length <= 100,** no BOM

- **Windows/WSL reality.** The fences run under the same WSL bash the merged

- `docs/state/merge_test_index.json`, `merge_history`, the WAL,
